subject: economics
title: Boardroom Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: You're a strategy consultant. Evaluate automation, productivity investment and the human cost of change.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics exam-style adventure on production: evaluation of automation, training and productivity policy.
final_note: Production strategy mastered. Banking and finance next!

concepts.def: Falling unit cost as output rises.
Workers/firms focus on a narrow task.

walkthroughs.body_html: 1) Capital investment — better machines. 2) Training — better human capital. 3) Better management — Toyota-style lean processes. Each has costs and time-lags. Top-band answers weigh ROI vs upfront costs.

Robots cut unit costs and raise quality but displace low-skill workers (structural unemployment). Long term, new jobs emerge in design and maintenance. Evaluation: depends on retraining, region, speed of change.
Use: time lag, cost, magnitude, distributional impact, and opportunity cost. Conclude with a justified judgement: which policy is most effective and why, in this context.

mcqs.q: Which is most likely to RAISE UK productivity in the long run?
options: Cutting training budgets
Investing in worker skills and new tech
Closing universities
Banning automation

mcqs.q: Falling unit costs as output expands is called?
options: Inflation
Economies of scale
Diseconomies of scale
Productivity puzzle

mcqs.q: How is economic growth shown on a Production Possibility Curve?
options: Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
By an outward shift of the entire curve — reflecting an increase in productive capacity through more or better resources, technology, or skills.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
Growth is shown by moving from inside the curve to a point on the curve.

mcqs.q: What causes the supply curve to shift?
options: Changes in production costs, technology, taxes/subsidies, number of producers, expectations — anything affecting supply other than the good's own price.
When demand rises, the supply curve shifts right to meet it.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
Supply shifts only when consumers want more.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
A change in price shifts the demand curve.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
